items.title: Akamai Report: AI-Driven Digital Deception Is Escalating Enterprise Fraud and Shrinking Phishing Lifespans
items.summary: Akamai's 2026 fraud and abuse research finds scams such as fake shops overtook classic credential phishing early in the year, and that commerce draws the largest share of login traffic, with a big slice of risky attempts being account-verification probes that precede credential stuffing. For teams defending logins and checkout, it argues for watching intent across the whole account lifecycle to catch slow, low-volume stuffing and card testing that rate limits miss.

items.title: Mastercard's Plans for a 'Turning Point' in Agentic Commerce
items.summary: Alongside strong quarterly results, Mastercard's chief executive said agent-driven shopping is already adding network volume and should keep growing through the holidays, while noting that issuers, processors and merchants are at very different stages of readiness for it. That readiness gap is the practical issue for payment engineers, since agent tooling and tokenized credentials only help if every hop in the authorization chain can recognize and handle agent-initiated transactions.

items.title: Elavon pursues Paze, agentic commerce
items.summary: Speaking at Money20/20, the head of a large merchant acquirer urged the industry to put safety ahead of speed as AI agents enter checkout, and said the bank-owned Paze wallet is ready for pilots despite the tough economics of past wallet wars. It frames a real tension for merchants and acquirers choosing between fast-moving tech-platform agent launches and slower bank-led wallet and trust frameworks.

items.title: Will ditching the 'honor all cards' rule matter?
items.summary: The proposed card-network settlement would let merchants decline or surcharge premium cards instead of accepting every card a network issues, but observers doubt many retailers will risk turning away high-spending customers. If the change survives court review, acceptance logic, surcharge disclosures and card-level routing at the point of sale could become new design decisions for merchant payment teams.

items.title: FTC, states sue Toast over fees
items.summary: Federal and state regulators accuse the restaurant point-of-sale and payments provider of hiding fees from merchants and diners, including a small charge on online orders, and of making subscriptions hard to cancel, which the company denies. The case signals rising enforcement attention on fee transparency across commerce payment stacks, from checkout line items to merchant contract terms.

items.title: Agentic payments for marketplaces: How a smart fridge can shop safely
items.summary: This engineering walkthrough builds an autonomous reordering agent on an agentic checkout protocol, with a deterministic policy engine that approves, escalates or denies each final basket and with spend authority granted through scoped, revocable payment tokens instead of raw card data. It is a concrete reference design for keeping LLMs out of the authorization decision, using bounded grants, idempotent retries and verified webhooks to make agent purchases safe.

items.title: Liability looms over AI shopping
items.summary: Bank and payments executives warn that purchases made by AI agents are spreading faster than the rules that decide who pays when something goes wrong, with competing protocols, narrow purchase-protection offers and no case law yet. For teams running disputes and fraud operations, unclear liability means agent-initiated transactions may need distinct flags, evidence capture and loss-allocation policies before volumes grow.

items.title: Fraudsters Leave Patterns, and AWS Wants AI to Follow Them
items.summary: The piece describes banks moving from static rules toward transaction foundation models and graph neural networks that track behavior sequences and links between accounts and devices, with agentic tools assembling investigation evidence while humans keep the final call. It offers a useful reference architecture for fraud ML teams weighing sequence and graph models against card testing, scams and synthetic identities.

items.title: Instacart to stop offering smart carts
items.summary: Instacart is winding down its Caper smart-cart hardware business after slow retailer adoption, taking a sizable charge and shifting its in-store push toward software, data and AI. The retreat is a signal for anyone planning in-aisle or cart-based checkout that hardware-heavy approaches face steep rollout economics compared with phone and lane-based options.

items.title: AI Recommendations Need a Checkout Shoppers Trust
items.summary: Survey data shows AI shopping assistants send many consumers to stores they have never used, yet most still complete the purchase on a familiar marketplace where payment details and protections are already stored. For commerce teams, it suggests that stored credentials, clear returns and dispute handling at checkout matter more than discovery in winning AI-referred sales.

items.title: How Stripe is designing Checkout for AI agents
items.summary: Stripe explains how it exposed its hosted checkout to AI agents through WebMCP, surfacing tools only when relevant to page state and reusing existing frontend logic, and reports agents finishing checkout faster with fewer tokens and tool calls. It is a concrete pattern for engineers deciding whether to build a separate agent checkout or make the existing one machine-readable.

items.title: Shoppers Are Turning Chargebacks Into a Customer Service Hotline, Justt Chargeback Benchmark Report Finds
items.summary: A two-year study of contested chargebacks across 165 merchants finds item-not-received and cancelled-subscription disputes nearly doubled their share to about a quarter, while fraud-coded disputes fell to roughly 60 percent; win rates on identical claims varied by 30-plus points depending on processor and issuer. Dispute teams may need evidence and automation tuned for service claims, and the partner-level variance argues for tracking representment outcomes by acquirer and issuer.

items.title: Socure links AI agents to verified people and businesses
items.summary: Socure introduced a suite that detects AI agents driving browser sessions, scores their trustworthiness across identity, authorization and risk signals, and binds agents to a verified principal through W3C verifiable credentials. It is another sign that risk stacks are adding an agent-identity layer, so fraud decisioning will increasingly need to ask who authorized an agent rather than only whether traffic is a bot.

items.title: Visa Credentials Reach 5.2 Billion as Network Expands Into Agentic Commerce
items.summary: Visa's fiscal fourth-quarter results show tokens now cover more than half of credentials and over 60 percent of e-commerce transactions, tap-to-pay at about three-quarters of U.S. in-person payments, and dozens of agentic-commerce partners in production with leadership naming trust as the main barrier. Token coverage at this level makes network tokens the default card-not-present path, and the agentic push signals more token-based delegation that risk and checkout systems must handle.

items.title: The Faster Payments Council Issues a Guide on Messaging
items.summary: The U.S. Faster Payments Council published operational guidance on non-value messages for instant payments, such as payment requests, returns, status reports and exception handling, as RTP and FedNow volumes keep climbing. Teams building on real-time rails can use it as a checklist for the exception and status flows that usually decide whether irrevocable payments are supportable in production.

items.title: Fed loses debit card cap appeal
items.summary: An Eighth Circuit panel affirmed a lower-court ruling that vacated the Federal Reserve's 21-cent debit interchange cap, finding the Fed may only count per-transaction incremental costs and must rewrite the standard. A lower cap would reshape debit acceptance economics and routing strategy for merchants and issuers alike, though a conflicting Sixth Circuit case keeps the final outcome uncertain.

items.title: USDA proposes adding chip and tap-to-pay tech to EBT cards
items.summary: A proposed USDA rule would require every state to issue SNAP EBT cards with EMV chip and contactless capability, and require authorized retailers to accept them within two years of finalization. Grocers and POS teams should plan terminal and certification work now, since moving off magstripe is aimed squarely at the skimming losses that have plagued benefit cards.

items.title: Retailers See Declined Payments but Miss the Second Chance to Save the Sale
items.summary: Survey data shows commerce firms apply intelligent retries to well under half of declined payments, roughly half the rate of finance and infrastructure firms, and that limited control over payment tokens sharply curbs automatic rerouting. It is a useful benchmark for teams weighing investment in retry logic, token portability and multi-processor routing to recover authorizations.

items.title: European Payments Firms Form Council for Agentic Commerce
items.summary: A group of European local payment schemes and processors has formed a council to define how consumers authorize AI agents, how banks verify them, how agents identify merchants, and how refunds and disputes work. It adds another standards track alongside network-led agent identity work, so builders of agentic checkout should expect to support local methods and multiple verification models.

items.title: AI and Deepfakes Are Streamlining Account Takeover Attacks
items.summary: New identity-verification data indicates a large share of failed fraud attempts involved forged identity documents, with AI and deepfakes making it easier for attackers to pose as real customers and get into established accounts. The takeaway for risk teams is that trust established at onboarding decays, so step-up checks and behavioral monitoring need to continue throughout the account lifecycle.

items.title: Chargebacks911 Launches First-of-Its-Kind AI Agent Purchase Indemnification for Merchants
items.summary: A dispute-management provider now offers an add-on that covers merchants against qualifying chargebacks on agent-initiated purchases, using behavioral and dispute history to decide which transactions are eligible. It signals that liability for AI-agent purchases is starting to be priced and transferred, which matters for anyone designing agentic checkout risk rules and dispute workflows.

items.title: 57% of Large Firms Report Bot or Agent Incidents or Losses
items.summary: A PYMNTS Intelligence survey of 350 fraud, risk and compliance leaders finds that larger companies are far more likely to report incidents or losses tied to bots and automated agents, and also see somewhat higher false-positive rates. It proposes a layered know-your-agent approach that verifies who an agent acts for and what it is permitted to spend, a useful framing for anyone designing controls for automated or agent-initiated traffic.

items.title: Shopping is Muse's top task: Meta
items.summary: Meta reported that shopping is the leading use of its Muse personal AI agent, with purchase volume high enough that its payments partner had to raise credit limits, even as some large banks move to block agent access to customer accounts. It offers an early real-world signal of agent-initiated payment volume, relevant to teams sizing capacity, limits and risk controls for agentic checkout flows.

items.title: Sam's Club Taps Affirm as Exclusive BNPL Provider
items.summary: Affirm signed a multi-year deal to be the sole buy now, pay later option at Sam's Club, starting online within weeks and expanding to stores in early 2027. The move shows warehouse and big-box retailers bringing installment payments into the physical checkout, which affects point-of-sale integration, tender mix and fraud controls for financed purchases.

items.title: 81% of Suspected Digital Fraud Attacks Target Existing Customer Relationships, TransUnion Finds
items.summary: A new TransUnion study finds that most suspected digital fraud in the first half of 2026 happened inside established customer relationships rather than at onboarding, with scams and authorized fraud named as a top loss driver and AI accelerating attack volume. For risk teams, it reinforces the case for continuous, post-login risk scoring and scam-aware controls instead of concentrating defenses at account opening.

items.title: Unauthorized AI Agents Have Accessed Bank Accounts at Top U.S. Banks
items.summary: Large U.S. banks have detected outside AI agents operating inside customer accounts, often using credentials customers handed over, and some have cut off agent access entirely while others weigh read-only modes. The episode shows how credential-sharing agents blur the line between legitimate automation and account takeover, pushing risk teams toward explicit agent identification and scoped, delegated permissions.

items.title: Q3 2026 Global Air Travel Fraud Report
items.summary: Accertify's quarterly analysis of roughly 123 million airline bookings shows prevented fraud rates climbing in many departure markets even as booking volumes fell, with sharp regional differences led by the Middle East, Africa and South Asia. Teams running card-not-present risk for travel or other high-ticket digital goods can use the regional baselines to tune geography-based rules and expect fraud pressure to hold up when legitimate demand softens.

items.title: Revolut outage disrupts online banking operations worldwide
items.summary: A widespread Revolut outage that knocked out its app, transfers and card-related services was traced to a power event at a single Google Cloud region in London. It is a sharp reminder for payment platform engineers to test regional failover and dependency concentration in their cloud footprint, since one zone or region failure can still take down customer-facing money movement.

items.title: At 12, Apple Pay Has Yet to Break the Card Habit In-Store
items.summary: A PYMNTS Intelligence survey of about 2,500 U.S. consumers finds mobile wallet use at the register has roughly doubled since 2023 but is still a small share of in-store purchases, with rewards loyalty keeping physical and tap-to-pay cards dominant. Retail payment teams can use the data to calibrate wallet acceptance and checkout investments, and to note that wallet usage tracks which card is loaded more than the wallet itself.

items.title: Treasury tallies $270M in suspicious financial aid transactions
items.summary: FinCEN says bank suspicious activity reports filed since its July alert surfaced about 270 million dollars in activity possibly tied to federal student aid fraud, built on stolen or synthetic identities posing as enrolled students and on paid straw applicants. Synthetic and borrowed identities that pass enrollment checks also pass account opening, so onboarding teams should watch for clusters of new accounts receiving government disbursements and moving the money out quickly.

items.title: Studies gauge fraud costs for banks, financial services
items.summary: Two new studies put numbers on fraud economics: LexisNexis Risk Solutions estimates U.S. financial firms now bear about 5.47 dollars in total cost per dollar lost, up from 4 in 2021, while a PYMNTS study finds institutions spend over 2 dollars on prevention per dollar that still slips through, with websites and apps driving most losses. The multiplier figures are useful for anyone building a business case for fraud tooling, since investigation, recovery and operational costs dwarf the direct loss line most dashboards track.

items.title: FTC Data Shows Investment Scams Fuel Fivefold Surge in Seniors' Fraud Losses
items.summary: FTC figures show reported losses by people aged 60 and over climbed roughly fivefold between 2020 and 2025 to about 3 billion dollars, driven largely by individual losses above 100,000 dollars from investment, romance and impersonation schemes. Large authorized transfers by long-tenured customers rarely trip classic fraud rules, which argues for scam-specific signals such as sudden large first-time payees and coached-session indicators.

items.title: ComCom caps interchange fees, promises $40 million savings
items.summary: New Zealand's competition regulator will cap interchange on Visa and Mastercard commercial credit card transactions from April 2027, estimating merchant savings of about 40 million dollars a year on top of earlier caps on consumer cards. Regulators are increasingly targeting the premium and commercial card tiers that carry outsized fees, so acceptance cost models and surcharging logic need to track card-category rules market by market.

items.title: Checkout.com Expands into In-Person Payments
items.summary: Long an online-only acquirer, Checkout.com is adding in-store acceptance by pairing its acquiring stack with terminals and point-of-sale software from Mollie, launching first in the UK and EEA with the U.S. to follow. More online-native processors moving into physical retail strengthens the push toward unified commerce, where one token vault, risk view and reporting stack covers both channels.

items.title: Securing your app, together
items.summary: Following a wave of compromised third-party apps that redirected shoppers to look-alike checkout pages, Shopify asked app developers to scan for unauthenticated routes, adopt expiring tokens, sanitize all rendered data and lock down accounts, and previewed tighter storefront script limits plus IP-restricted API keys. It is a reminder that the checkout supply chain extends to every script and configuration endpoint a merchant installs, so payment page integrity monitoring and least-privilege app access matter as much as the processor integration.

items.title: What happens when AI agents start paying each other? Watch Mastercard Agent Pay for Machines in action
items.summary: Mastercard demonstrated agents buying digital services from each other using the x402 pattern, where a service answers with a payment-required response and the agent signs an off-chain voucher within a preset budget that can be batched and settled later in fiat or stablecoins, and opened early access to its APIs and sandbox. Machine-to-machine micropayments change the shape of authorization and risk, shifting controls toward per-agent spending mandates, voucher verification and aggregated settlement instead of one card authorization per purchase.

items.title: Paze sets big targets after revamp
items.summary: The bank-consortium wallet Paze is aiming to win over the hundred largest U.S. merchants within three years after its relaunch, citing strong transaction growth and roughly 220 million enrolled cards. A bank-backed checkout button competing with phone and processor wallets could shift how merchants weigh wallet acceptance, tokenized credentials and checkout-page real estate.

items.title: Broadcom launches Arcot Scam Defense for payment fraud detection
items.summary: Broadcom added a capability to its Arcot 3-D Secure platform that scores card-not-present authentications for signs of a scam in progress, such as device location mismatches, slow passcode entry and an active phone call on the authenticating device. It highlights that a passed step-up challenge is no longer proof of a legitimate purchase when the real cardholder is being coached, pushing authentication teams to treat session context as a fraud signal.

items.title: Booking.com Probe Exposes Travel Fraud Beyond Checkout
items.summary: The European Commission is examining how scammers reach travelers through a large booking platform, including compromised hotel partner accounts and messaging channels used to push guests toward fake payment pages. The case shows how account takeover on the merchant or partner side can turn genuine order data into convincing scam lures, so marketplace operators need to protect partner logins and outbound payment requests, not only checkout.

items.title: Your AI agent can move money in Stripe - here's how to stay in control
items.summary: Stripe walks through the guardrails for letting AI agents act on a payments account, from user confirmation of sensitive writes over MCP to agent-tagged API keys whose refunds and payouts can be routed to human approvers via webhooks. It is a concrete pattern for anyone exposing money-moving APIs to autonomous software: give agents distinct identities, gate high-risk actions behind review, and make pending approvals observable.

items.title: New payment rails catch on, slowly
items.summary: Speakers at Money20/20 described slow uptake of instant payments and stablecoins, citing legacy systems, skepticism and fatigue with adding yet another rail, while firms mix ACH, instant transfers, stablecoins and even checks depending on cost and recipient. For payment platform builders this argues for multi-rail orchestration and routing logic rather than betting on one new rail replacing the rest.

items.title: Fiserv taps AI for retail rethink
items.summary: A Fiserv executive says merchants are deciding whether legacy commerce stacks can absorb AI shopping agents or whether new stacks are needed, and expects fully autonomous agent purchases to require extra records proving user intent and payment details. That points to new data fields and evidence trails flowing between merchants, acquirers and networks, which will shape authorization payloads and dispute handling for agent-initiated orders.

items.title: Visa changes fees in Canada
items.summary: Visa is cutting interchange for Canadian small merchants below a sales threshold starting October 24 and will add a per-transaction processor fee on domestic Canadian transactions from April 2027, while Mastercard has not widened its small-business program. Simultaneous rate cuts and new network fees show why acceptance cost models and pricing engines need regular updates as network rules shift by market.

items.title: Automation to Accountability: Governing AI in Fraud and Disputes
items.summary: Drawn from an industry webinar, this piece looks at how institutions should oversee AI used in fraud investigations and dispute handling as new state rules raise expectations for transparency and human oversight. It is a practical reminder that dispute and fraud models need continuous drift monitoring, documented decision logic and override tracking, not a one-time sign-off.

items.title: Banks' Growing Fraud Tech Stacks Create an Integration Challenge
items.summary: Survey findings indicate financial institutions have piled up many fraud tools and now struggle to make them act as one defense, with system complexity cited as the main barrier and most in-house builders still mixing in third-party products. Because scams increasingly arrive through legitimate logins, the value now lies in joining signals across the whole customer and payment journey, which is an architecture and data-plumbing problem as much as a modeling one.

items.title: Britain seeks to break Apple's grip on contactless payments
items.summary: The UK competition regulator proposed lower access fees and host card emulation access to the iPhone NFC chip so rival wallets can compete with the incumbent tap-to-pay option, with consultation open until mid-November. If adopted, merchants and issuers could see more wallet choices at the terminal in the UK, adding new token and wallet types that acceptance and risk systems must recognize.

items.title: AI's Democratizing Bent Is Quickly Affecting Fraud Rates and Perpetrators
items.summary: Coverage of a Socure consumer survey finds a meaningful share of respondents admit using AI to commit some form of fraud, most often first-party abuse, and that organized rings lean on AI more than individuals. Lowering the skill barrier means risk teams should expect more first-party and synthetic-identity attempts from people with no prior fraud history, which weakens signals built on past behavior.

items.title: Nacha Reports More Faster Payments Gains
items.summary: Third-quarter ACH figures show overall network volume growing modestly while same-day ACH volume jumped by more than a third and passed a trillion dollars in value for the quarter. Faster settlement on existing rails compresses the window for catching bad payments and pushes teams to rethink return handling, risk holds and reconciliation timing.

items.title: Agentic Commerce Is Still Hype Ahead of Reality
items.summary: An analyst view argues that AI-agent shopping is still in its infrastructure phase and will account for only a sliver of transaction value even by 2030, with discovery changing faster than payment flows. For builders, it suggests prioritizing agent identification and authorization standards steadily rather than rushing wholesale checkout rewrites.

items.title: Utah forms digital ID consortium
items.summary: Utah announced a multi-state group to set shared governance principles for state-issued digital IDs built around user control of identity data, with several more states expected to adopt similar frameworks. As mobile driver licenses spread, they could become a stronger verification input for onboarding and account recovery, provided standards for sharing and consent settle.

items.title: Hackers Exploit Open Banking Services to Test Stolen Credentials Without Paying a Cent
items.summary: Researchers at Group-IB found a scam-as-a-service crew abusing a legitimate spend-management app's account-linking flow to check whether stolen bank and card credentials were live, leaving the platform to pay the open-banking verification bill, and then using the same app's notifications to send marketplace-themed phishing. It shows that onboarding and account-linking steps can become a free validation oracle for fraudsters, so new-account behavior, first instrument links and early outbound messaging deserve the same velocity controls as checkout.

items.title: TransUnion Debuts New Scoring Capability to Combat Fraud
items.summary: TransUnion introduced scores aimed at synthetic identities and credit washing that lenders can use directly in adverse-action decisions, with reason codes they can give to declined applicants. Explainable identity-risk signals that are usable in regulated decisions point toward fraud models that must justify outcomes, not just rank risk, which matters for anyone designing identity verification and account-opening controls.

items.title: Google Mandates Further Verification for US and Canada Financial Ads
items.summary: Google will extend its financial services advertiser verification program to the US and Canada in early 2027, requiring advertisers of certain financial products to prove they are authorized by regulators or recognized registries. Fake financial ads are a common entry point for investment and impersonation scams, so tighter controls upstream may shift where scam traffic originates and how payment providers see it arrive.

items.title: Matera, Payfinia and Solana Foundation Demonstrate New U.S. QR Code Payment Standard at Money20/20
items.summary: A group of vendors gave the first public live demo of the ANSI X9.150 QR standard, where a single invoice code can be settled over FedNow, RTP or a stablecoin rail and the invoice updates automatically, with open-source reference software released alongside. A shared QR payload across rails could simplify how merchants and banks integrate instant payments, though the demo is not a product and adoption is still at the pilot stage.

items.title: Swipe fees add nearly $320 million to consumers' Halloween costs, merchants group says
items.summary: A merchant coalition estimates that card acceptance fees will add roughly 319 million dollars to projected Halloween spending and uses the figure to push Congress toward the Credit Card Competition Act and its second-network routing mandate. The seasonal messaging signals continued legislative pressure on interchange and routing alongside the pending settlement fight, which could eventually reshape debit and credit routing logic at checkout.

items.title: Zero-Sum by Design: 10 Years of Uber's Payments Platform
items.summary: Uber's engineers look back on a decade of their payments platform, built on immutable money-movement records, double-entry bookkeeping that must always net to zero, an asynchronous Kafka pipeline and a workflow engine for in-session payments. It is a useful reference for anyone designing ledgers and payment orchestration at scale, especially on how generic abstractions for products and instruments kept the core stable as new payment methods were added.

items.title: 21% of Financially Stressed Grocery Shoppers Use Digital Wallets
items.summary: PYMNTS survey data show financially stressed grocery shoppers are far more likely than others to pay with a digital wallet (21% vs 8%) and to buy groceries online, with their wallet use roughly doubling since early 2024. A growing wallet and online mix changes the fraud and authorization profile at grocery checkout.

items.title: Skyfire and Forter Team to Strengthen Agentic Commerce Decisioning
items.summary: Forter is feeding Skyfire's know-your-agent data into its fraud decisions so merchants can verify both the AI agent placing an order and the person it acts for. Agent identity is quickly becoming a first-class risk signal alongside device and account data.

items.title: When Identity Documents Leak, Verification Has to Change
items.summary: Using a reported insider leak of about 680 Revolut customers' KYC files as the hook, Sift argues that a genuine stolen passport plus selfie can pass document checks. Verification needs to layer device, behavioral and network-linkage signals and keep re-scoring identity over time, especially for enrollment and account recovery.

items.title: Scaling Radar: Fighting fraud with agent-assisted machine learning
items.summary: Stripe trained its Radar fraud model on about 11 billion transactions and cut epoch time by 80%, then rolled back because immature labels (disputes arrive weeks later) made the bigger dataset worse. It also explains how AI agents now run feature and training experiments on its shared offline and online feature platform, with human checkpoints.

items.title: Retailers warned fraud & disputes may stretch into new year
items.summary: Chargebacks911 warns that an earlier start to holiday shopping widens the fraud window, and that refund abuse and chargebacks from peak-season sales keep arriving well into the first quarter. Merchants estimate about a quarter of returns are abusive, so December fraud numbers alone understate the real cost.

items.title: Your Fraud Team's New First Responder: Introducing the Sift Fraud Attack Defense Suite
items.summary: Sift launched an attack-detection agent that baselines each customer's own traffic and alerts on BIN velocity, low-value transaction surges, chargeback spikes and registration bursts, using statistical methods rather than generative AI. Its alert set is a practical checklist for card-testing and velocity monitoring.

items.title: Self-checkout restrictions open a new lane for lawsuits
items.summary: An employment lawyer explains how Long Beach's self-checkout ordinance, now copied by other California cities, sets staffing ratios and a 15-item limit for grocery and drug stores and lets customers or employees sue per violation. Spreading local rules like these could change how retailers design and staff self-checkout.

items.title: PAX Enlists Wink's Face and Palm Checkout at the Point of Sale
items.summary: PAX is building Wink's face and palm recognition into its point-of-sale apps so enrolled shoppers can pay or be recognized for loyalty on camera-equipped terminals, with liveness checks against spoofing. Biometric checkout adds a new identity signal at the register, along with new spoofing risks.

items.title: Stripe agentic commerce revs up
items.summary: Stripe's John Collison said agent-driven purchase activity climbed steeply from September, without giving numbers, while Amazon has blocked Meta's Muse assistant from shopping on its site. The contrast frames the build-or-block choice large retailers face on agent traffic.

items.title: Accertify tallies agentic checkout
items.summary: Accertify separated AI-assisted browsing from fully autonomous agent purchases and found the latter is still a tiny fraction of transactions in its data. A useful reality check on how much agent-placed order volume merchants are actually seeing today.

items.title: AmEx's Next Step for Agentic Commerce Is a Framework; Forter's Agentic Verification Move
items.summary: American Express outlined a four-step design for capturing a shopper's approved purchase intent, proving it, binding an agent credential to it, and presenting that proof at authorization. A concrete sketch of how intent data could flow through card authorization for agent-initiated payments.

items.title: Forter Turns the AI Shopping Agent Surge Into a Secure Revenue Channel for Merchants
items.summary: Forter released an Agentic Commerce Engine for verifying AI shopping agents and handling headless checkout, saying agent-placed orders on its network quadrupled since August while bots posing as assistants doubled. A view into how fraud vendors are productizing agent traffic ahead of the holiday peak.

items.title: Mastercard Advances Agentic Commerce With New Trust and Intelligence Services
items.summary: Mastercard is piloting a US score that estimates whether an AI agent initiated a purchase, the first piece of an intelligence layer for its Agent Pay framework, with Cloudflare and Skyfire helping on agent identity. A network-provided agent signal like this could become a standard input to transaction risk models.

items.title: A Judge Rules an Apple Pay Fee Case Can Move Forward As a Class Action
items.summary: A federal judge certified a class of US card issuers suing Apple over Apple Pay fees and its exclusion of rival contactless wallets from the iPhone. If the case loosens Apple's control of NFC, merchants could see competing in-store wallets and different tap-to-pay economics.

items.title: Building an anomaly detection platform at DoorDash to catch fraud trends early
items.summary: DoorDash's fraud team runs a daily batch job that aggregates fraud metrics across thousands of segment combinations, applies a windowed z-score test against a lagged baseline, and clusters flagged segments for analysts. A practical, easy-to-copy template for catching emerging fraud trends early.

items.title: The Friday Checkout: Ahold Delhaize's digital disaster is a customer retention nightmare
items.summary: A cybersecurity incident kept Ahold Delhaize's US grocery sites and apps down for a week, so shoppers could not log in or redeem loyalty rewards and online orders moved to third-party delivery apps. A sobering case study in how much customer trust rides on identity and account systems during an incident.

items.title: Scams Capture 22.4% of Fraud Dollars as Banks Adjust Defenses
items.summary: A PYMNTS Intelligence survey of 90 US financial institutions finds scams nearly doubled their share of fraud losses year over year, while credential-based account takeover remains the largest single category. A good reminder that access checks alone miss authorized but manipulated activity.

items.title: Visa, Mastercard urge court to approve swipe-fee settlement
items.summary: A final-approval hearing is set for next month on the Visa and Mastercard swipe-fee settlement. It would let merchants decline some premium and commercial credit cards, a break from the long-standing honor-all-cards rule.

items.title: Visa-Mastercard payouts top $631M
items.summary: Close to 690,000 merchants have now been paid from the interchange damages settlement, with more than five billion dollars still in the fund. A hearing on the separate injunctive-relief deal, which Walmart and others oppose, is set for next month.

items.title: Mastercard to introduce offline payment rules across Europe
items.summary: After the 2025 Iberian blackout, Mastercard will require new European cards from February 2027 and new terminals from May 2027 to support offline approvals with chip-stored limits of up to 200 euros. A real-world example of designing card acceptance for network loss, and of the fraud tradeoffs of approving offline.

items.title: How agentic payments present risk
items.summary: This opinion piece argues that Regulation E, Regulation Z and network zero-liability policies leave it unclear who absorbs the loss when an AI agent exceeds what a consumer allowed, and proposes machine-readable records of an agent's authority. That gap will shape dispute volumes and liability for agent-placed orders.

items.title: Fine-tuning LLMs for risk assessment
items.summary: Stripe engineers fine-tuned a 4B open-weight model on text-serialized account records using only review labels, derived a risk score from label-token probabilities, and report sizable precision gains over prompting and over XGBoost on several risk tasks. A concrete recipe to weigh against classic gradient-boosted models.

items.title: Riskified Launches Agent Identity Risk Intelligence
items.summary: Riskified is adding tooling that detects when an AI assistant is placing an order or contacting support, ties it back to a real consumer identity and returns a live risk score, with a merchant beta in December and broad release in 2027. Another sign that agent identity scoring is moving into mainstream fraud tools.

items.title: Owning Intelligence Series, Part 1: How Coinbase Built, Evaluated, and Post-Trained a Fraud Agent
items.summary: Coinbase describes an LLM risk agent that sits after its existing ML model and rules for guest checkout, can only add blocks, and cut fraud meaningfully in a 50 percent traffic test. Replays later showed newer model versions catching less fraud than older ones, a strong argument for replay-based regression tests on every model upgrade.

items.title: October 2026 interchange and network updates
items.summary: A rundown of this month's card network changes, including Mastercard's higher decline service fee and Visa moving response code 57 into its never-approve reattempt program. Both matter for anyone maintaining authorization retry logic.

items.title: Visa's Compelling Evidence 3.0 changes on 24 October: prior purchases can come from other merchants
items.summary: From October 24, merchants fighting Visa 10.4 card-absent fraud disputes may cite a cardholder's earlier undisputed purchases at other merchants, matching tokens, and login IDs from agentic payment providers. Pre-arbitration evidence stays limited to data the acquirer itself processed, so dispute evidence pipelines may need updating.

items.title: The agentic payments stack in 2026: what Visa, Stripe and Mastercard shipped
items.summary: A builder's rundown of agent tokens, agent-to-agent fraud checks and scoped credentials from the card networks and Stripe. The common thread is that no agent gets unrestricted card access, which shapes how agent-initiated orders will be scored.

items.title: Walmart and Sam's Club add Tap to Pay at checkout
items.summary: Walmart is rolling out contactless payments to all US stores and clubs by the end of 2026 and to fuel stations by mid-2027. A notable shift for one of the last big holdouts on mobile wallets.

items.title: Retail payment trends in 2026: what's shaping checkout
items.summary: Seven trends shaping retail checkout this year: agentic commerce, account-to-account payments, wallets, surcharging and dual pricing, and network tokenization. A quick orientation piece.

items.title: Signifyd's 2026 State of Fraud Report: account takeover, card testing and BOPIS fraud all jump
items.summary: Across thousands of merchants, fraud pressure rose about a third year over year in early 2026, with account takeover up 78% and card testing up 175%. Buy-online-pick-up-in-store fraud rose 65%, putting store pickup and login protection in focus.

items.title: Mastercard bolsters scam defense with new acquirer monitoring program
items.summary: Mastercard now requires acquirers to act within three days on flagged scam activity at their merchants, following Visa's VAMP program. Both networks are pushing more fraud responsibility onto merchants and their processors.

items.title: Fraud fight can't wait on government
items.summary: A merchant consultant argues retailers should tighten dispute management now rather than wait on the Fed, FTC and Treasury fraud roundtable. Friendly fraud and chargebacks are the main cost he highlights.

items.title: Cell-Based Architecture for Resilient Payment Systems
items.summary: An American Express distinguished engineer explains splitting a payment platform into isolated cells so a bad deploy or failure only affects a slice of traffic. A clear walkthrough of blast-radius thinking for any high-availability payment service.

items.title: Recorded Future annual payment fraud report: AI raises the scale of attacks
items.summary: Mastercard's threat-intelligence unit reports scammers using AI marketing tools to target victims the way a legitimate business would. Its advice is to fuse cyber and fraud intelligence and move from reactive to predictive defenses.

items.title: Debit card fraud losses rise, especially card-not-present
items.summary: A Kansas City Fed analysis of 2021 to 2023 data shows card-not-present debit fraud kept climbing while card-present fraud rates diverged between dual- and single-message networks. A useful baseline for online debit risk.

items.title: How we built it: Stripe Radar
items.summary: An older but still useful look at the design decisions behind Stripe's ML fraud system: features, model choices and lessons learned. Good background for anyone building a fraud model platform.

items.title: Payment processing architecture in 2026: what to know
items.summary: Covers five architecture decisions for modern payment platforms, including treating network tokenization as a design choice rather than a compliance task, and planning for agent-initiated checkout. Vendor-written, but a decent checklist.
